core_obligations: Reduce the converse to finite purely inseparable test extensions: the direction (1) implies (2) is clear, and assuming (2) it suffices by the finite inseparable criterion to show that X_{k''} is reduced at every point x'' over x for each finite purely inseparable k''/k (proof lines 506-508, 520-521).

Compare over a common extension: choose a common extension k''' of k'' and k' and a point x''' of X_{k'''} lying over both x'' and x'; the induced map of local rings O_{X_{k''}, x''} -> O_{X_{k'''}, x'''} is a flat local homomorphism, hence faithfully flat (proof lines 509-516).

Descend reducedness: by assumption the local ring on the right is reduced because x''' lies over x' and X_{k'} is geometrically reduced at x', so faithful flatness forces O_{X_{k''}, x''} to be reduced; since k'' was an arbitrary finite purely inseparable extension, the criterion gives that X is geometrically reduced at x (proof lines 516-521).
proof_roadmap: The forward implication is immediate from the definition; for the converse, fix a finite purely inseparable k''/k and a point x'' over x (proof lines 506-508).
Install a common extension k''' over both k'' and k', pick x''' over both x'' and x', and use faithful flatness of the resulting local ring map (proof lines 509-516).
Deduce reducedness at x'' from reducedness at x''' via descent, and conclude geometric reducedness at x by the finite inseparable criterion (proof lines 516-521).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that geometric reducedness of X over k at a point x is equivalent to geometric reducedness of the base change X_{k'} at every point x' over x, for an arbitrary field extension k'/k, and deduces the global statement (statement lines 492-502). The forward direction is by definition; the converse cannot be done by a single base change, because the definition tests all field extensions, so the proof replaces that by the finite purely inseparable ones and compares each of them with k' over a common extension k''', where the resulting local ring map is flat and local, hence faithfully flat, allowing reducedness to descend (proof lines 509-519). The two reduction devices, the finite inseparable criterion and faithful flatness descent, are the content. The claim is H2.
